<!--
Starter parameterized report (Python engine).

Render (ALWAYS inside the project env so Quarto uses .venv, not /opt/python):
  uv run quarto render report-template.qmd
  uv run quarto render report-template.qmd -P year:2025 -P dept:11 \
      -P data_uri:s3://<bucket>/data/2025/dept=11/*.parquet

The `_environment` file (QUARTO_PYTHON=.venv/bin/python) is a safety net for a
bare `quarto render`, but Quarto only reads it inside a project (a `_quarto.yml`
at the root) — so prefer `uv run` anyway. Data is STREAMED from S3 (skill
onyxia-storage-s3), never read from a hard-coded local path, and every figure
below is COMPUTED from that data — never transcribed or hard-coded.
-->

```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]
# Default values — overridden by -P at render time
year = 2024
dept = "31"
data_uri = ""
```

## Context

This report covers department `{python} dept` for year `{python} year`.

```{python}
#| label: load-data
import os
import polars as pl

# ---- Stream data from S3 first (Onyxia rule, skill onyxia-storage-s3) --------
# Read lazily / in memory from S3; only `aws s3 cp` to local disk if a tool
# truly needs a file. Endpoint from the injected AWS_S3_ENDPOINT — never
# hard-code credentials.
if data_uri:
    storage_options = {"aws_endpoint": f"https://{os.environ['AWS_S3_ENDPOINT']}"}
    df = pl.read_parquet(data_uri, storage_options=storage_options)
    # Large data → scan lazily and let predicate/column pushdown trim it:
    #   df = (pl.scan_parquet(data_uri, storage_options=storage_options)
    #           .filter(pl.col("dept") == dept)
    #           .collect())
else:
    # Placeholder so the *template* renders out of the box. DELETE this branch
    # and pass -P data_uri:s3://... for a real report.
    # NEVER hard-code result figures here — they must come from the data.
    df = pl.DataFrame({"category": ["A", "B", "C"], "value": [12, 7, 21]})

n_rows = df.height
total = df["value"].sum()
```

Loaded **`{python} n_rows`** rows; total value **`{python} f"{total:,}"`**.

## Key figure

```{python}
#| label: fig-values
#| fig-cap: "Value by category (computed from the data)"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Draw in the cell and let Quarto capture it via plt.show().
# Do NOT use IPython.display.Image and do NOT savefig + ![](path.png) here.
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar(df["category"], df["value"])
ax.set_xlabel("Category")
ax.set_ylabel("Value")
plt.show()
```
